title: Weddings, festivals & occasions
goal: Invite and be invited, find your way through a Sindhi wedding, give the right wishes and blessings, and take part in Eid, Ramzan, urs fairs, Cheti Chand and Diwali.
intro:
Sindh celebrates a lot, and loudly: three-day weddings with **ڍول** and **لاڏا**, two Eids, Ramzan iftars, the great **عرس** fairs at Sufi shrines, and the Hindu Sindhi festivals of **چيٽي چنڊ** and **ڏياري**. Every one of them comes with its own words — and its own wishes.

In this unit you'll learn the blessing forms Sindhi uses all the time — **الله توهان کي وڏي ڄمار ڏئي**, **شل سدائين خوش رهو**, **آباد رهو!** — which are built on the **subjunctive** you met in unit 18, and the ways to insist that someone *must* come: **ضرور اچجو**, **متان دير ڪرين!**

grammar.title: Wishes and blessings: الله … ڏئي، شل …، آباد رهو
grammar.body:
Blessings use the **subjunctive** — the present tense without ٿو (unit 18): ڏئي، رکي، ڪري، رهو. On its own it means *may …*:

**الله + person + کي + thing + subjunctive** — 'may God give / keep …':
الله توهان کي وڏي ڄمار **ڏئي** 'may God give you a long life'
الله توهان کي خوش **رکي** 'may God keep you happy'
الله اوهان جو جوڙو سلامت **رکي** 'may God keep you both well'
الله شفا **ڏئي** 'may God heal (you)' (unit 9)

**الله ڪري ته …** 'God grant that …, I do hope …' + subjunctive: الله ڪري ته توهان جلدي ٺيڪ **ٿيو**.

**شل** + subjunctive 'may …!': **شل** خوش **رهو** 'may you be happy', شل سدائين آباد **رهو**. Elders say this to the young.

**Imperative-style blessings**, especially to newly-weds and children: **آباد رهو!** 'prosper!', **خوش رهو!** 'be happy!'. The polite subjunctive (-o) looks exactly like the polite imperative — so a blessing sounds like a friendly command.

**Congratulations**: **X مبارڪ!** or **X مبارڪ هجي!** (one thing) — عيد مبارڪ، سالگرهه مبارڪ، شادي مبارڪ هجي. **مبارڪون هجن!** (plural) is the all-purpose 'congratulations!'; on something: X **جون** مبارڪون.

**Replies:** to a blessing say **آمين** 'amen'; to any مبارڪ say **خير مبارڪ** 'thank you, and the same to you'; add **توهان کي به** 'you too'.

examples.native: الله ڪري ته توهان جلدي ٺيڪ ٿيو.
examples.roman: allāh kare ta tavhāṃ jaldī ṭhīku thiyo.
examples.en: I do hope you get well soon. (lit. God grant that you become well quickly)

examples.native: عيد مبارڪ! — خير مبارڪ، توهان کي به!
examples.roman: ʿīda mubārak! — xair mubārak, tavhāṃ khe bi!
examples.en: Eid Mubarak! — Thank you, and to you too!

grammar.title: 'Be sure to …': ضرور اچجو، ياد سان، متان
grammar.body:
In Sindh you never just mention an invitation — you insist, and the guest promises. The tools:

**ضرور + -jo form** 'be sure to, do …': **ضرور اچجو** 'do come', **ضرور ٻڌائجو** 'be sure to let us know'. The -jo form (unit 18) is warm and points to the future, which is exactly right for invitations.

**ضرور + 'have to'** (unit 15) for a stronger push: توهان کي **ضرور اچڻو آهي** 'you absolutely must come'.

**ياد سان** 'remember to, without fail': **ياد سان** مٺائي کڻي اچجو 'remember to bring sweets'. **'Don't forget'**: نه وسارجو.

**متان** (unit 21) 'make sure you don't …, don't you dare …' + subjunctive: **متان** دير **ڪرين**! (friend) / متان دير **ڪريو**! (polite). The verb after متان is positive — متان itself carries the 'don't'.

The guest's side: **ضرور ايندس / اينداسين، انشاءالله**. If you can't come, apologise and bless: معاف ڪجو، نه اچي سگهنداسين — الله خوش رکي!

examples.native: شادي ڇنڇر تي آهي، ضرور اچجو.
examples.roman: shādī chhanchhara te āhe, zarūr achijo.
examples.en: The wedding's on Saturday — do come.

examples.native: توهان کي ضرور اچڻو آهي، نه ته امان ناراض ٿيندي.
examples.roman: tavhāṃ khe zarūr achaṇo āhe, na ta amāṃ nārāzu thīndī.
examples.en: You simply have to come, or Mum will be upset.

dialogue.title: A Hyderabad wedding
dialogue.setting: Ali invites his colleague John, who is learning Sindhi, to his sister's wedding in Hyderabad. Then, on the wedding day, John meets the groom and Ali's grandmother.

lines.speaker: Ali
lines.native: جان، هي وٺ — منهنجي ڀيڻ جي شاديءَ جو ڪارڊ.
lines.roman: jān, hī vaṭhu — munhinjī bheṇa jī shādīa jo kārḍu.
lines.en: John, here — my sister's wedding invitation.

lines.speaker: Ali
lines.native: خميس تي مهندي، جمعي تي نڪاح ۽ بارات، ۽ آچر تي وليمو.
lines.roman: xamīsa te mehndī, jumʿe te nikāhu ai bārāta, ai āchara te valīmo.
lines.en: Mehndi on Thursday, the nikah and baraat on Friday, and the walima on Sunday.

lines.speaker: John
lines.native: ٽي ڏينهن؟! مان ته رڳو هڪ سوٽ کڻي آيو آهيان!

lines.en: Three days?! I've only brought one suit!

lines.speaker: Ali
lines.native: ڪا ڳالهه ناهي! مهنديءَ تي اجرڪ ۽ ٽوپي پائجانءِ — اسان جي طرفان تحفو.
lines.roman: kā ɠālhi nāhe! mehndīa te ajraka ai ṭopī pāijāṃi — asāṃ jī tarafāṃ tohfo.
lines.en: No problem! Wear an ajrak and a Sindhi cap to the mehndi — a present from us.

lines.speaker: Ali
lines.native: عورتون لاڏا ڳائينديون، ڍول وڄندو، ۽ سڀ نچندا. متان شرم ڪرين!
lines.roman: ʿauratūṃ lāɗā ɠāīndyūṃ, ḍholu vaʄando, ai sabhu nachandā. matāṃ sharmu kareṃ!
lines.en: The women sing lada songs, the dhol plays and everyone dances. Don't you dare be shy!

lines.speaker: John
lines.en: (On Friday) What do I say to the groom?

lines.speaker: Ali
lines.native: چئو ‘شادي مبارڪ هجي’، ۽ هٿ ۾ سلامي ڏي.
lines.roman: chao ‘shādī mubārak huje’, ai hatha meṃ salāmī ɗe.
lines.en: Say 'congratulations on your wedding', and put a money gift in his hand.

lines.speaker: John
lines.native: شادي مبارڪ هجي، ادا! الله اوهان جو جوڙو سلامت رکي.
lines.roman: shādī mubārak huje, adā! allāh avhāṃ jo joṛo salāmatu rakhe.
lines.en: Congratulations, brother! May God keep you both well.

lines.speaker: Groom
lines.native: خير مبارڪ! واهه، توهان ته سنڌي ڳالهايو ٿا!
lines.roman: xair mubārak! vāh, tavhāṃ ta sindhī ɠālhāyo thā!
lines.en: Thank you! Wow, you speak Sindhi!

lines.speaker: Ali's grandmother
lines.native: شل خوش رهين، پٽ! الله تو کي وڏي ڄمار ڏئي.
lines.roman: shala xushu raheṃ, puṭa! allāh to khe vaɗī ʄamāra ɗie.
lines.en: Be happy always, son! May God give you a long life.

culture:
A Sindhi wedding usually runs over several days. At the **مهندي** the bride's and groom's sides sing **لاڏا** and **سهرا** to the **ڍول**, henna is applied, and the groom's family often turn up in matching **اجرڪ** and **سنڌي ٽوپي**. Then come the **نڪاح**, the **بارات** (in traditional Sindhi **ڄڃ**), the tearful **رخصتي** when the bride leaves her parents' home, and the **وليمو**. Guests give **سلامي** — cash in an envelope or pressed into the hand — rather than boxed presents, and elders give it to children too. The usual wish is **شادي مبارڪ هجي**; older people bless the couple with **آباد رهو** and **الله جوڙو سلامت رکي**.

**Ramzan** changes the rhythm of life: offices close early, everyone rushes home for **افطاري**, and inviting friends to iftar is a big part of social life. If someone is fasting, don't eat or drink in front of them. **ننڍي عيد** (Eid al-Fitr) means new clothes, visits and **عيدي** for children; at **وڏي عيد** (Eid al-Adha) families do **قرباني** and share the meat with relatives and the poor. The reply to every **عيد مبارڪ** is **خير مبارڪ**.

Sindh's Sufi shrines hold huge **عرس** fairs: Lal Shahbaz Qalandar at Sehwan, with its ecstatic **دمال** (dhamaal) drumming; Shah Abdul Latif at Bhit Shah, with all-night singing of his poetry; Sachal Sarmast at Daraza. Sindhi Hindus celebrate **چيٽي چنڊ**, the birthday of the river saint **جهوليلال** and the Sindhi New Year, as well as **ڏياري** and **هولي**, and many Muslim friends join in with sweets and greetings. And on **Sindhi Culture Day** (the first Sunday of December), the whole province wears ajrak and topi.

tip.title: Be sure to come!
tip.body:
- **ضرور + -jo**: ضرور **اچجو** 'do come'.
- Stronger: توهان کي ضرور **اچڻو آهي** 'you must come'.
- **متان** + subjunctive = 'don't you dare': متان دير **ڪرين**! (the verb stays positive).
- Reply: ضرور **اينداسين**، انشاءالله.

tip.title: Wedding words
tip.body:
- **گهوٽ** = groom, **ڪنوار** = bride — real Sindhi words; you'll also hear دولهه / دلهن.
- **سلامي** = money you give the couple (or children), not a boxed present.
- 'Looks …' = **پيو / پئي لڳي**: ڪنوار سهڻي **پئي لڳي**.
- 'Started to …' = infinitive + **لڳڻ**: سڀ **نچڻ لڳا**.

sentences.en: The bride looks gorgeous! The groom too!

sentences.roman: ghoṭa khe salāmī ɗiyaṇī āhe.
sentences.en: I need to give the groom a money gift.

sentences.en: The women are singing wedding songs.

lessons.title: Blessings and good wishes

tip.title: May God …: blessings
tip.body:
- Blessings use the **subjunctive** (present without ٿو): الله توهان کي خوش **رکي** 'may God keep you happy'.
- **شل** + subjunctive = 'may …!': شل خوش **رهو**.
- To newly-weds: **آباد رهو!**
- Reply to a blessing: **آمين**; to مبارڪ: **خير مبارڪ**.

lessons.title: Ramzan and the two Eids

tip.title: Festival greetings
tip.body:
- Any occasion + **مبارڪ**: رمضان مبارڪ، عيد مبارڪ. Reply: **خير مبارڪ**.
- **ملهائڻ** = to celebrate: عيد ڪيئن **ملهائيندا** آهيو؟
- Fasting? **توهان جو روزو آهي؟** — then don't eat or drink in front of them.

new: توهان کي ۽ سڄي گهر کي عيد مبارڪ!

sentences.native: اڄ اسان وٽ افطاريءَ تي اچو.
sentences.roman: aʄu asāṃ vaṭi iftārīa te acho.
sentences.en: Come over to ours for iftar today.

sentences.native: منهنجي عيدي ڪٿي آهي؟ چاچا، پنج سؤ کان گهٽ نه!
sentences.roman: munhinjī ʿīdī kithe āhe? chāchā, panja sau khāṃ ghaṭu na!
sentences.en: Where's my Eidi? Uncle, no less than five hundred!

sentences.native: ٻارن کي عيدي ملي ۽ اهي ڏاڍا خوش ٿيا.
sentences.roman: ɓāran khe ʿīdī milī ai uhe ɗāḍhā xushu thiyā.
sentences.en: The children got their Eidi and were thrilled.

sentences.native: وڏي عيد تي اسين قرباني ڪندا آهيون.
sentences.roman: vaɗī ʿīda te asīṃ qurbānī kandā āhyūṃ.
sentences.en: At Eid al-Adha we do the sacrifice.

sentences.native: توهان عيد ڪيئن ملهائيندا آهيو؟
sentences.roman: tavhāṃ ʿīda kīeṃ malhāīndā āhyo?
sentences.en: How do you celebrate Eid?

sentences.native: ادا، توهان کي ۽ سڄي گهر کي عيد مبارڪ!
sentences.roman: adā, tavhāṃ khe ai saʄe ghara khe ʿīda mubārak!
sentences.en: Brother, Eid Mubarak to you and the whole family!

sentences.native: هن سال عيد ڳوٺ ۾ ملهائينداسين.
sentences.roman: hin sāla ʿīda ɠoṭha meṃ malhāīndāsīṃ.
sentences.en: This year we'll celebrate Eid in the village.

sentences.native: ڀٽ شاهه تي عرس ڪڏهن آهي؟
sentences.roman: bhiṭ shāh te ʿursu kaɗahiṃ āhe?
sentences.en: When is the urs at Bhit Shah?

sentences.native: عرس تي هزارين ماڻهو ايندا آهن.
sentences.roman: ʿursa te hazārīṃ māṇhū endā āhin.
sentences.en: Thousands of people come to the urs.

sentences.native: چيٽي چنڊ جون مبارڪون، ادا! اڄ ڪٿي ٿا وڃو؟
sentences.roman: cheṭī chanḍa jūṃ mubārakūṃ, adā! aʄu kithe thā vaño?
sentences.en: Happy Cheti Chand, brother! Where are you off to today?

sentences.native: ڏياريءَ تي اسين پاڙيسرين کي مٺائي ڏيندا آهيون.
sentences.roman: ɗiyārīa te asīṃ pāṛesiryan khe miṭhāī ɗīndā āhyūṃ.
sentences.en: At Diwali we give sweets to the neighbours.

sentences.native: سالگرهه مبارڪ! ڪيڪ ڪٿي آهي؟
sentences.roman: sālgirahi mubārak! keku kithe āhe?
sentences.en: Happy birthday! Where's the cake?

sentences.native: ڪيڪ ڪير کڻي آيو؟
sentences.roman: keku ker khaṇī āyo?
sentences.en: Who brought the cake?

sentences.native: پاس ٿيو آهين؟ ته پوءِ مٺائي کڻي اچ!
sentences.roman: pāsu thiyo āhīṃ? ta poi miṭhāī khaṇī achu!
sentences.en: You passed? Then bring us some sweets!

sentences.native: سيوهڻ ۾ لعل شهباز قلندر جو عرس ڏاڍو وڏو ٿيندو آهي.
sentences.roman: sehvaṇa meṃ lāl shahbāz qalandar jo ʿursu ɗāḍho vaɗo thīndo āhe.
sentences.en: Lal Shahbaz Qalandar's urs at Sehwan is huge.
